Если вашего вуза нет в списке, сильные анкеты также рассматриваются индивидуально.\n\nНужно ли уже вести блог?\n\nНет. Компания открывает приём заявок на новый сезон программы «Амбассадоры Сбера в вузах». С 2020 года выпускниками этой программы стали студенты 40 университетов.\n\n...\n\nПрограмма рассчитана на студентов 2-го курса бакалавриата и старше, включая магистрантов и аспирантов. \n\nКлючевые критерии отбора — активная жизненная позиция, навыки организации мероприятий, умение создавать контент и презентовать идеи. \n\nАмбассадоров ожидают: ежемесячная стипендия, фирменный мерч, доступ к обучающим курсам Сбера и наставничество от экспертов компании, возможность посещать закрытые и внутренние мероприятия и расширять профессиональные контакты.\n\n...\n\nВ этом году программа охватит 19 городов: Москву, Санкт-Петербург, Новосибирск, Екатеринбург, Казань, Нижний Новгород, Красноярск, Самару, Ростов-на-Дону, Омск, Краснодар, Воронеж, Пермь, Владивосток, Хабаровск, Иркутск, Кемерово, Рязань и Иннополис. \n\nЧтобы стать участником, нужно подать онлайн-заявку, выполнить творческое задание (видеопрезентация до 1,5 минут и пост для соцсетей) и пройти финальное интервью с экспертами Сбера — обсуждение мотивации и плана работы.\n\nВ задачи амбассадора входят продвижение карьерных и образовательных проектов компании в своем вузе, ведение контента в социальных сетях и помощь команде Сбера в проведении мероприятий\n\nПодать заявку на программу «Амбассадоры Сбера в вузах» можно до 20 июля 2025 года, а первые амбассадоры приступят к работе уже в сентябре\n\n---\n\nTitle: Ambassadors registration - SberGraduate\nURL: https://sberstudent.ru/ambassadors-registration/\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\nAmbassadors registration - SberGraduate\n\n## Заверши регистрацию\n\n обязательно для заполнения \n\nСколько часов ты готов уделять задачам амбассадора в неделю?\n\nТвой вуз (начни набирать название в справочнике. Не стало исключением и высшее образование. Представьте, что вузы могут автоматизировать рутинные задачи, упростить доступ к информации, повысить уровень взаимодействия с абитуриентами и студентами, а также укрепить свой имидж как современного учебного заведения.\n\nСегодня это не просто мечта — это реальность, которую открывает проект AI-помощник для вузов на основе GigaChat. На конференции AI Journey его представила команда Сбера, и этот инструмент уже готов изменить образовательный процесс.\n\n...\n\nAI-помощник интегрируется в существующую инфраструктуру вуза через API. С помощью технологий обработки естественного языка он понимает и отвечает на запросы, используя актуальные данные. Например, студенту нужно узнать расписание экзаменов — помощник моментально предоставляет информацию.\n\n...\n\nAI-помощник также облегчает работу преподавателей и административного персонала, сводя к минимуму необходимость\n\n...\n\n### Как подключить AI-помощника в своем вузе?\n\n### Шаг 1. Формирование команды\n\nСоберите команду из заинтересованных преподавателей, сотрудников и студентов, готовых решать задачи разметки данных и разработки решений. Рекомендуемый состав:\n\n1. Разметчики: готовят данные, персонализируют решения и оценивают их качество.\n2. Разработчики: пишут парсеры, настраивают генерации и внедряют собственные решения.\n\nЕсли вы преподаватель — обсудите проект с коллегами и студентами, согласуйте участие с руководством вуза. Если студент — обратитесь к преподавателю или в администрацию.\n\n### Шаг 2. Подача заявки\n\nСвяжитесь с нашей командой по указанным контактам. Мы наладим канал коммуникации и назначим контактное лицо. После включения вашего вуза в проект выдадим уникальный токен для обращений в техническую поддержку.\n\nEmail: UniAssistant@sberbank.ru\n\nTelegram: @giga_education_support_bot\n\n### Шаг 3. Ознакомление с документацией\n\nВнимательно изучите предоставленную документацию и пошаговый план действий. Все материалы доступны по ссылке.\n\n### Шаг 4. Регистрация на платформах\n\nКачество ответов помощника напрямую зависит от корректности подготовки данных. Вся работа по разметке ведется на платформе TagMe. А в репозитории на GitHub представлен шаблонный проект для упрощения и персонализации сбора данных по вашему вузу.\n\n- TagMe: зарегистрируйтесь для выполнения задач разметки данных. Подготовьте список email-адресов участников для добавления в систему.\n- GitHub: зарегистрируйте разработчиков и передайте их никнеймы для доступа к репозиторию.\n\n### Шаг 5. Подготовка данных\n\n1. Составьте список релевантных источников информации для вашего вуза (страницы сайта, основные документы, социальные сети, сервисы вуза, студенческие и вузовские СМИ)\n2. Определите подходящие страницы и данные, на основе которых будет строиться ответ AI-помощника. \n3. Оба этапа реализуются на TagMe.\n\n...\n\n### Шаг 8. Внедрение\n\nПосле достижения качества ответов (не менее 85%) AI-помощника для вашего вуза решение будет включено в основной проект. Интегрируйте решение через API в существующую инфраструктуру своего вуза. Это может быть веб-форма на сайте, отдельная страница или канал в мессенджерах. Например, шаблон бота для Telegram представлен в Документации.\n\n...\n\n### Готовы присоединиться?\n\nAI-помощник для вузов — это шаг в будущее для вашего вуза. Подключив его, вы получите:\n\n- Упрощение административной работы.\n- Возможности для разработки новых проектов и аналитики.\n- Улучшение имиджа и повышение привлекательности для абитуриентов и студентов.\n\nПрисоединяйтесь к цифровой трансформации высшего образования с AI-помощником для вузов на основе GigaChat уже сегодня! А мы поможем вам на каждом этапе подключения, по всем вопросам можно обратиться через: \n\nEmail: UniAssistant@sberbank.ru \n\nTelegram: @giga_education_support_bot"

Rather than reinventing the wheel, Project Aquarium fosters collaboration across academia, industry, and communities to build on existing efforts. It also emphasizes cultural data, safety, and responsible practices to ensure alignment across global languages, especially those that remain underrepresented. The platform will initially strengthen resources for Southeast Asian regional languages spoken by more than 700 million people, including Burmese, Khmer, Thai, Malay, Indonesian, Filipino, Tamil, and Lao.\n\n...\n\n### A Call for Global Collaboration\n\nBuilding inclusive AI cannot be done by a single organization or research team. It targets organizations that require transparent, inspectable models that can be self-hosted, adapted, or integrated into existing infrastructure without dependence on closed APIs. StableLM sits in the category of foundation models for NLP and generation, alongside other transformer-based Large Language Model (LLM) architectures (machine learning / GenAI).\n\nThe project’s primary purpose is to provide developers and enterprises with models that handle core language tasks such as text generation, question answering, summarization, code assistance, and dialogue (NLP / application development). Stability AI distributes StableLM model weights under open terms, together with usage guides and technical documentation, enabling organizations to evaluate, benchmark, and customize the models for domain-specific scenarios. Multiple parameter scales are offered so teams can select configurations that match their compute budgets, latency constraints, and deployment environments (model serving / infrastructure planning).\n\nFrom an architectural perspective, StableLM follows transformer-based LLM designs (deep learning / model architecture). The models are trained on large text corpora curated by Stability AI and partners, with pretraining objectives that support downstream fine-tuning and instruction-tuning. Enterprises can use common frameworks such as PyTorch or compatible inference runtimes to load and serve the models, integrate them into microservices, or run them in containerized and orchestration environments (MLOps / deployment automation).\n\nIn enterprise contexts, StableLM is used as a base model for building chatbots, virtual assistants, content generation tools, developer productivity utilities, and knowledge retrieval interfaces when combined with Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines (applications / knowledge management). Because weights are available, organizations can apply fine-tuning and alignment techniques to adapt StableLM to internal terminology, compliance language, or task-specific workflows. This aligns the project with broader Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) practices such as model versioning, evaluation, and continuous improvement pipelines (model governance / lifecycle management).\n\nStableLM interoperates with the broader Stability AI ecosystem, which also includes models for image and other media modalities, allowing multi-model architectures where StableLM handles text understanding, orchestration, and control logic (multimodal AI / orchestration). For directory and taxonomy purposes, StableLM is best categorized as an open-source, transformer-based LLM family for enterprise and developer use, suitable for deployment in on-premises (on-prem), cloud, and hybrid environments where control over data, inference behavior, and integration patterns is required (enterprise AI / platform capability).\n\nOur description of StableLM. Updated February 2026.\n\n...\n\n## At a glance\n\nMaintainer\nStability AI\n\nRepository\nstability.ai\n\n---\n\nTitle: Stability AI launches StableLM, an open source ChatGPT alternative\nURL: https://forum.devtalk.com/t/stability-ai-launches-stablelm-an-open-source-chatgpt-alternative/106325/1\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n# Stability AI launches StableLM, an open source ChatGPT alternative\n\nURL: https://forum.devtalk.com/t/stability-ai-launches-stablelm-an-open-source-chatgpt-alternative/106325\nCategory: In The News\nTags: chatgpt, via-ars-technica, in-the-news\nCreated: 25 April 2023 01:57 UTC\nPosts on this page: 1\nShowing post: 1\n\nAuthor: @CommunityNews\nPost date: 25 April 2023 01:57 UTC\n\n> StableLM’s 3B and 7B models are available now on GitHub under CC 4.0 license.\n\nRead in full here:\n\n> Stability AI launches StableLM, an open source ChatGPT alternative\n> \n> StableLM's 3B and 7B models are available now on GitHub under CC 4.0 license.\n\n---\n\nTitle: Campus Crew Program | Power Up Your Campus with HackerRank\nURL: https://www.hackerrank.com/campuscrew\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\nCampus Crew Program | Power Up Your Campus with HackerRank\n\n# Power Up Your Campus\n\nHost hackathons, guide peers, and build a stronger developer community as a HackerRank ambassador\n\n## About the program\n\nCampus Crew is HackerRank’s selective student ambassador program. conclusions and reusable methods.\n\n> Turn Your Experience into Impact.\n\n## 👋 How to Participate​\n\nWhether you've built a runnable application with the MiniCPM series, or distilled reusable See Academic email requirements below.\n- Own a GitHub personal account.\n- Are at least 13 years old.\n\n## What documents can I use to prove I'm a student?\n\n- A picture of your school ID with current enrollment date\n- Your class schedule\n- Your transcript\n- An affiliation or enrollment verification letter\n\n## Academic email requirements\n\nGitHub's verification process is individually tailored. When the system detects that recent applicants from your school successfully verified using their academic email, future applicants from the same school must also use an academic email.\n\n### Your school requires an academic email address\n\nIf the application asks for an academic email, you must add and verify one on your GitHub account before applying. See Adding an email address to your GitHub account.\n\n### Your school does not provide an academic email address\n\nIf your institution does not issue academic emails, provide official documentation, such as a school webpage or a letter on school letterhead, explaining the policy. Then reapply for GitHub Education.\n\n### Your school's email domain is not recognized\n\nIf your school email domain is not recognized in the application, contact GitHub Education Support with your school's full name, website URL, and the email domain you are attempting to use.\n\n## Applying to GitHub Education\n\n1. Navigate to your Education benefits settings.\n2. Under \"GitHub Education\", click Start an application.\n3. Supports:\n\n- exact and approximate nearest neighbor search\n- single-precision, half-precision, binary, and sparse vectors\n- L2 distance, inner product, cosine distance, L1 distance, Hamming distance, and Jaccard distance\n- any language with a Postgres client\n\nPlus ACID compliance, point-in-time recovery, JOINs, and all of the other great features of Postgres\n\nHave a lot of vectors?     "content": "Title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated ...\nURL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793\nPublished: 2024-11-11T00:00:00.000Z\nAuthor: John Yang\nHighlights:\n# SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering\n\n John Yang * Carlos E. Jimenez * Alexander Wettig Kilian Lieret Affiliation: Affiliation: Shunyu Yao Karthik Narasimhan Ofir Press Affiliation: Affiliation: Princeton Language and Intelligence, Princeton University \n\n###### Abstract\n\nLanguage model (LM) agents are increasingly being used to automate complicated tasks in digital environments. Just as humans benefit from powerful software applications, such as integrated development environments, for complex tasks like software engineering, we posit that LM agents represent a new category of end users with their own needs and abilities, and would benefit from specially-built interfaces to the software they use. We investigate how interface design affects the performance of language model agents. As a result of this exploration, we introduce SWE-agent: a system that facilitates LM agents to autonomously use computers to solve software engineering tasks. SWE-agent’s custom agent-computer interface (ACI) significantly enhances an agent’s ability to create and edit code files, navigate entire repositories, and execute tests and other programs. We evaluate SWE-agent on SWE-bench and HumanEvalFix, achieving state-of-the-art performance on both with a pass@$1$ rate of $12.5$% and $87.7$%, respectively, far exceeding the previous state-of-the-art achieved with non-interactive LMs. Finally, we provide insight on how the design of the ACI can impact agents’ behavior and performance.\n\n...\n\nFrom this effort, we introduce SWE-agent, an agent composed of an LM and ACI, that can interact with a computer to solve challenging real-world software engineering problems, such as those proposed in SWE-bench [20]. In contrast to the Linux Shell’s granular, highly configurable action space, SWE-agent’s ACI instead offers a small set of simple actions for viewing, searching through and editing files. The ACI uses guardrails to prevent common mistakes, and an agent receives specific, concise feedback about a command’s effects at every turn. We show that ACIs tailored specifically for LMs outperform existing user interfaces (UIs) designed for human users, such as the Linux shell.\n\n...\n\nHere we describe how SWE-agent provides an ACI for LMs to act as software engineering agents, enabling them to effectively search, navigate, edit, and execute code commands. The ACI comprises several principal components, including search/navigation, file viewer, file editor, and context management. At each step, SWE-agent generates a thought and a command, then incorporates the feedback from the command’s execution in the environment (ReAct; Yao et al. [62]). Built atop the Linux shell, SWE-agent also allows access to common Linux commands and utilities when needed.\n\n---\n\nTitle: shibam dhar\nURL: https://linkedin.com/in/shibamdhar\nPublished: 2026-10-06T05:50:24.000Z\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n# Shibam Dhar\n\nDynamic Developer Relations Manager with a proven track record in enhancing product experiences, fostering community growth | DevRel Eng @harness.io | EX Microsoft Learn Student Ambassador | MVP’26 @ Alibaba Cloud\n\nBengaluru, Karnataka, India (IN)\n\n...\n\nBeyond\n\n...\n\n### [Harness](https://www.linkedin.com/company/harnessinc)\n\n#### Senior Developer Relations Engineer (Current)\n\nMay 2026 - Present (5 months) in Bengaluru, State of Karnataka, India\n\nDepartment: Engineering and Technical • Level: Senior\n\n#### Developer Relations Engineer (Current)\n\nJun 2025 - Present (1 year and 1 month) in Bangalore Urban, State of Karnataka, India\n\nI work at the intersection of product, engineering, and customer enablement across multiple platform capabilities, including the Internal Developer Portal, Artifact Registry, and AI Test Automation. The process involves:\n\n1. Optimal Routing: Finally, it routes the query to the appropriate model, balancing cost and performance.\n2. Model Capability Matching: It then matches these queries with the capabilities of various models.\n3. Analyzing Query Characteristics: The system first evaluates the characteristics of incoming queries.\n\nThis approach is meticulously designed to ensure high-quality responses while significantly reducing operational costs.\n\n### Demonstrated Results\n\nThe RouteLLM framework has been tested using public data from Chatbot Arena, yielding impressive results:\n\n- Open-Source and Accessible: All code and datasets are publicly available, inviting collaboration and further innovation.\n- Efficient Performance: On MMLU and GSM8K, the cost savings were 45% and 35%, respectively, compared to using only GPT-4.\n- Cost Reduction: On the MT Bench, RouteLLM achieved over 85% cost reduction, while still delivering 95% of GPT-4’s performance.\n\n---\n\nTitle: RouteLLM Reviews\nURL: https://slashdot.org/software/p/RouteLLM/\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n# RouteLLM Reviews\n\n### LMSYS\n\nWrite a Review\n\nAlternatives\n\nClaim this page\n\n## Go to About page\n\n## RouteLLM Description\n\nCreated by LM-SYS, RouteLLM is a publicly available toolkit that enables users to direct tasks among various large language models to enhance resource management and efficiency. Guardrails (or \"rails\" for short) are specific ways of controlling the output of a large language model, such as not talking about politics, responding in a particular way to specific user requests, following a predefined dialog path, using a particular language style, extracting structured data, and more.\n\nThis paper introduces the NeMo Guardrails library and contains a technical overview of the system and the current evaluation.\n\n...\n\n## Installation\n\nTo install using pip:\n\n```bash\n> pip install nemoguardrails\n```\n\nFor more detailed instructions, see the Installation Guide.\n\n...\n\nThe NeMo Guardrails library enables developers building LLM-based applications to add **programmable guardrails** between the application code and the LLM.\n\n...\n\n- **Building Trustworthy, Safe, and Secure LLM-based Applications:** you can define rails to guide and safeguard conversations; you can choose to define the behavior of your LLM-based application on specific topics and prevent it from engaging in discussions on unwanted topics.\n\n- **Connecting models, chains, and other services securely:** you can connect an LLM to other services (a.k.a. tools) seamlessly and securely.\n\n...\n\nTo add programmable guardrails to your application you can use the Python API or a guardrails server (see the Server Guide for more details). Using the Python API is similar to using the LLM directly. Calling the guardrails layer instead of the LLM requires only minimal changes to the code base, and it involves two simple steps:\n\n1. Loading a guardrails configuration and creating an `LLMRails` instance.\n2. Making the calls to the LLM using the `generate`/`generate_async` methods.\n\n...\n\nThe library includes guardrails for LLM self-checking (input/output moderation, fact-checking, hallucination detection), NVIDIA safety models (content safety, topic safety), jailbreak and injection detection, and integrations with community models and third-party APIs. For the complete list, see the Guardrails Library documentation.\n\n...\n\n## Inviting the community to contribute\n\nThe example rails residing in the repository are excellent starting points. We enthusiastically invite the community to contribute towards making the power of trustworthy, safe, and secure LLMs accessible to everyone. For guidance on setting up a development environment and how to contribute to the NeMo Guardrails library, see the contributing guidelines.\n\n---\n\nTitle: CONTRIBUTING.md\nURL: https://github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo-Guardrails/blob/f2d44928/CONTRIBUTING.md\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\nWelcome to the NeMo Guardrails contributing guide. Now a third‑year computer science student in the College of Engineering, Ho has turned that philosophy into entrepreneurship, student leadership, and a string of high‑profile internships, culminating this summer with a software engineering role at Apple.\n\n...\n\nEntrepreneurship is the throughline of Ho’s college experience, most clearly reflected in Arctex, the startup he founded after identifying how time‑consuming college and scholarship applications can be. Arctex’s College App Assist automates repetitive application fields, allowing students to apply faster with a single click. The idea grew directly out of his own experience.\n\n“When I was applying to colleges and scholarships, I kept thinking, ‘There has to be a faster way to do this,’” Ho said. “I was spending five to ten hours per application just re‑entering the same information.”\n\nThe platform has attracted nearly 2,000 users and gained traction through OSU’s entrepreneurial ecosystem, including the Startup Hub. Mentorship, pitch competitions, and startup programming helped him refine both the product and his confidence as a founder. ... “It’s about\n\n...\n\nThat same impulse — to build and to share — has shaped Ho’s involvement in student organizations. During his first year at OSU, he served as vice president of BeaverHacks, OSU’s hackathon club, helping lead a rebrand and expand the club’s reach through larger, in‑person events. Unusually, Ho became an organizer before competing in college hackathons himself.\n\n“I actually learned how hackathons worked from the inside before I ever participated as a competitor,” he said. “It gave me a really good perspective on how community, sponsorships, and projects all come together.”\n\nNo longer an organizer of the club, he participated in BeaverHacks 2026 this May. His team snagged a first-place finish in the competition’s Hardware Track with their project Training Rails, a machine learning model to detect rail defects in real time.\n\n...\n\n### Creating community through hackathons and student leadership\n\nHo has also served as an officer in the Google Developer Club, where he led technical workshops and presentations for fellow students. Teaching and mentoring others became a recurring theme, reinforced through his work as a teaching assistant for an introductory computer science course.\n\nBeyond campus leadership, Ho pursued hands‑on industry experience early. At OSU’s Center for Applied Systems and Software (CASS), he worked as a student software engineer, developing a full‑stack system for a medical manufacturing supply chain.\n\n“That was my first real taste of software engineering on a team,” he said. “I got to work with product managers, UX designers, and other developers, and see how all the pieces fit together.”\n\n### From Groq to Apple\n\nHe then joined Groq as an application engineering intern, building tools and applications for enterprise clients—sometimes presenting them live at hackathons or company events. “It was my first time building applications quickly and putting them in front of real clients,” Ho said. “That was incredibly exciting.”\n\nThis summer, Ho will take the next step as a software engineering intern on Apple’s Core OS team. He initially became aware of the opportunity through his participation in the Lime Connect fellowship, a national program supporting high‑achieving students with disabilities. As one of just 25 undergraduate fellows, Ho, who has a hearing deficit, traveled to New York to connect with peers and alumni and gain insight into navigating the tech workforce.\n\n“Lime Connect was huge for me,” he said. “Meeting other students with disabilities and hearing from alumni made me feel like I wasn’t navigating this path alone.”\n\n---\n\nTitle: Contact | Groq is fast, low cost inference.\nURL: https://home.cloud.groq.io/contact\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n## Developer Support\n\nExplore our Community resources, or use the chat feature on GroqCloud Dev Console for support.\n\n## Enterprises\n\nInquire with our team about your inference use case.\n\n## Press / Media / Analysts\n\nPlease reach out to us at pr-media@groq.com and provide the following:\n\n- Key topic or theme\n- Information about you and your outlet\n- The timeframe of your request and any pressing deadlines\n- The name(s) of any specific Groqster you would like to involve\n\n## Social Media\n\nGroq is active on the following social outlets\n\nX – Real-time information for our community of developers and beyond\n\nLinkedIn – A connection space for our business community\n\nYouTube – Our video content including demos, feature updates, and Groq use cases\n\nThreads – Real-time updates and thought leadership from Groq\n\nInstagram – Our lifestyle channel featuring our amazing and talented Groqsters\n\n## Groq Headquarters​\n\n2700 Zanker Road, Suite 150 San Jose, CA 95134\n\n---\n\nTitle: Careers - Humain is Fast AI Inference\nURL: https://groq.humain.ai/careers/\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n# Groq Hires Exceptional Talent\n\nAt Groq, we believe AI will change humanity forever, and that making it affordable and universally accessible is the key to human agency in an AI economy. Educate 雲端校園大使計劃，自 2020 年起，已累計七屆、培育超過 168 位校園大使，影響超過 20,000 名學生學習 AWS。入選者將與一群來自全台各大專院校的未來雲端人才以及 AWS 策略方案部緊密合作，推廣 AWS 活動以及相關教育資源，包含 AWS Educate 平台、AWS Academy 平台、AWS 雲端知識與技術、以及其他跨部門合作機會，加入 AWS 在六個月的雲端之旅，你可以學到...\n\n1. 實際參與 AWS 台灣策略方案部門以及跨部門的合作經驗\n2. 參與不同專業領域實作機會 (如: 數位行銷、雲端技術、技術教學)\n3. 熟悉學習 AWS 企業文化，以及了解科技業工作模式\n4. 優先參加各類型 AWS 舉辦及協辦的活動、講座及研討會\n5. 獨立舉辦近百人活動，培養領導決策能力以及公開演說技巧 \n\n## 雲端校園大使任務\n\n1. 與來自不同校系的團隊成員一同策畫、執行【 AWS Educate 第三屆證照陪跑計畫 】，舉辦各類實作工作坊、技術/職涯講座。\n2. 在校園內至少協助一場與 AWS 技術/證照/教育平台相關的推廣活動，協助接洽校內行政單位、教師、學生，推廣 AWS 學習資源。\n3. 在校園內推廣 2026 AWS 黑客松，分享雲端知識、報名資訊，提高黑客松知名度。\n4. 畢業前進行校園大使計畫的最終培訓績效總結與成果發表。\n5. 任務編制依據專長分為「活動規劃」、「技術支援」、「行銷推廣」三種職能專長\n\n## 報名資格\n\n1. 國內公私立大專院校之在校學生 (至少在未來半年保有學生資格，且任職期間於台灣就讀) 不限科系、背景、年級\n2. 對雲端產業有興趣，想更深入認識雲端科技\n3. 對辦活動有熱忱，從發想到執行到優化，有獨當一面的領導力\n4. 有一顆好奇的心，喜歡嘗試不同的事物，樂於接受挑戰\n5. 有責任感且細心，願意投入每周 4-5 小時完成雲端大使之任務\n\n### Event Planning\n\n1. 有舉辦實體活動經驗者\n2. 有社團活動或幹部經驗者 (請附上幹部證明於備審資料)\n3. 活潑外向，喜愛結交新朋友且樂於分享\n\n### Technical Support\n\n1. 有 AWS 雲端操作實務經驗者\n2. 有修習相關課程或擁有專案經驗者\n3. 了解 AWS 雲端服務與產業知識\n4. 具備 AWS 相關證照 (請附上證明連結於申請動機)\n\n### Marketing\n\n1. 文字表達能力佳並有管理粉絲團或是社群行銷經驗\n2. 有經營自媒體或社群經驗者 (請附上社群/媒體連結於備審資料)\n3. 熟悉任一製圖軟體者\n\n## 報名流程\n\n1. 註冊 AWS These resources are concentrated in a handful of corporations and universities, and the models, data, and methods behind much of the resulting work are unavailable to researchers outside them. We do not believe that a small, elite circle should have a monopoly on the ability to do influential research.\n\nEleutherAI works to widen that circle. We release models, datasets, code, and methods so other researchers can inspect, reproduce, and extend our work, and we do that work in the open, where anyone can follow along and contribute. But public artifacts are not enough: researchers also need compute, mentorship, and the chance to lead work of their own. Our community reaches across more than thirty countries to train aspiring researchers, provide resources to those without them, and grow them into independent researchers in their own right.\n\nWe also help independent research communities build capacity of their own. Through shared compute and collaboration, new groups can pursue their own questions and publish openly. The goal is not to bring every promising group inside EleutherAI, it is for more researchers and organizations to set their own agendas, contribute work others can build on, and stand on their own. Several communities featured below began with that support.\n\n## Summer of Open AI Research (SOAR)\n\nEvery year EleutherAI holds SOAR, a 5-week fully online research internship program. We invite people with little research experience to contribute to open science under the mentorship of experienced researchers from our staff and broader community.\n\n## Support for Other Communities\n\nOpen science is a community effort. We partner with organizations around the world interested in growing open science and provide a variety of forms of support, including fiscal sponsorship, grants, computing resources, and technical support for their research. If your organization is interested in partnering with us, please reach out to contact@eleuther.ai\n\n...\n\n### Multi-Agent Security Initiative \n\nThe prominence of AI agents is growing rapidly, but work on multi-agent security and safety is lagging severely behind. Founded by Ben Hagag and Michael Mulet, MASI is focused on multi-agent security as a field of its own by studying how the presence of multiple interacting agents changes the AI safety and security landscape.\n\n Thought Virus: Viral Misalignment via Subliminal Prompting in Multi-Agent Systems →\n\n...\n\n## Communities We Have Supported\n\nWe helped these communities get started, and they have since grown into independent organizations with work and communities of their own.\n\n...\n\nEleutherAI members organize\n\n---\n\nTitle: EleutherAI\nURL: https://eleuther.ai/\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\nEleutherAI\n\n# Independent AI Research, Done in the Open\n\nWe build open-source AI infrastructure, pioneer interpretability and open-weight safety, and help researchers without frontier-lab resources do frontier work.\n\n...\n\n### Open-Weight Safety →\n\nOnce model weights are public, safeguards cannot rely on API monitoring or on post-training methods that fine-tuning can remove. We work on safety methods that remain effective when anyone can inspect and modify the model, which in practice means intervening in the training data and the training process.\n\nDeep Ignorance is one such method. It filters hazardous material out of pretraining data so that the model never learns it, and the resulting safeguard is substantially more resistant to adversarial fine-tuning than post-training alternatives. With FAR.AI we co-organize the Open-Weight Pretraining Safety Accelerator, which gives researchers access to the pretraining runs needed to test interventions of this kind at scale.\n\n...\n\nWe also study evaluation itself. This includes when benchmarks saturate and stop distinguishing between models, how the age of a benchmark affects comparisons across models, and how results should be reported so that they can be compared across groups. Through the EvalEval Coalition, which we co-founded with Hugging Face and the University of Edinburgh, we work on shared evaluation infrastructure with other institutions.\n\n---\n\nTitle: Eleuther AI site | Get Involved\nURL: https://researcher2.eleuther.ai/get-involved/\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\nEleuther AI site | Get Involved\n\n# EleutherAI \n\n## Get Involved\n\nWe welcome contributors of all backgrounds and experience levels! Please ask in the relevant discord channels if you think you can help out with any of the above.\n\nUnfortunately we do not have many projects that are accessible to people who are beginners at deep learning. We welcome you to hang out in our Discord and learn, and may have jobs you can help with from time to time, but we have many more beginners than beginner-friendly tasks.\n\n#### UI/UX\n\nWe have sporadic need for UI/UX work. Post in #website on Discord if you can help.\n\n#### Web Development and Graphic Design\n\nWe sporadically need help with various tasks related to managing our intnet presence. Neuropixels probes were developed through an international collaboration funded by the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI), Wellcome Trust, Gatsby Charitable Foundation and Allen Institute for Brain Science. Probes were designed, developed and fabricated at imec, Leuven Belgium in collaboration with HHMI Janelia Research Campus, Allen Institute for Brain Science, and University College London.\n\n## Getting Started\n\n1\n\nJoin the Discord\n\nThe Neuropixels Discord is your go-to hub for real-time peer support, troubleshooting tips, and the latest announcements from developers. Please use this invite to get access to Discord. (Previously Slack)​\n\n2\n\nSelect your configuration\n\nNeuropixels probes come in several versions—1.0, 2.0, NHP, and NXT—each designed for different recording needs. Review the specifications for probes, data acquisition systems, and software on the Technology page to find the right fit for you. Choosing the right configuration upfront saves time and ensures your data quality meets your experimental goals.\n\n3\n\nOrder hardware and tools\n\nOnce you have settled on a probe, place your order through Neuropixels.org or an authorized distributor. Don't forget the full kit: headstage, flex cable, and a PXI or OneBox acquisition system.\n\n4\n\nParticipate in a training\n\nNew users are encouraged to attend one of the regularly organized user workshops or training courses prior to using the probes. Courses are currently offered by the Allen Institute and University College London through a grant by the Wellcome Trust and generously supported by the Sainsbury-Wellcome Centre. Past trainings have been recorded for future use. Under the guidance of notable professors like Mitesh Khapra, Dr Anoop Kunchukuttan, and Dr Pratyush Kumar, AI4Bharat has a strong history of residents conducting cutting-edge research and publishing in renowned venues such as ACL, Interspeech, ICASSP, EMNLP, TMLR, and more. \n\nCollaborating with AI4Bharat researchers, residents have contributed to impactful open-source datasets and models like Samanantar, BPCC, IndicTrans1 and 2, IndicWav2Vec, IndicBart, IndicNLG Benchmark, widely adopted in government and industry.\n\nThe ideal candidate should be a recent graduate with a bachelor's degree in computer science or related fields from 2022 onwards and should have excellent programming skills demonstrated through independent projects on platforms like GitHub or Kaggle, with participation in competitive programming considered advantageous. \n\nA solid understanding of deep learning fundamentals, obtained through online courses with formal certification or as part of the B.Tech curriculum, is also required. Candidates should also have experience in training and evaluating large deep learning models, particularly on Transformer-based models for NLP such as BERT, mT5, mBART, wav2vec, and more. \n\nAlso Read NVIDIA Launches Open-Weight Transcription Model for 40 Languages\n\nHowever, an important point to note is that applications are only accepted from individuals willing to relocate to Chennai, except in exceptional circumstances.\n\nThe research lab recently launched Chitralekha, an open-source AI-powered video transcreation platform created in collaboration with EkStep. This platform incorporates a comprehensive workforce management system, facilitating end-to-end transcreation of videos from one language to another. There are no hard rules on how we verify users. In general, contributions should be based on your personal experience with Sensu.\n\n### Where do you ship? \n\nWe currently only ship swag to North America. Alternative rewards are available to verified users in other countries.\n\n### How can I check my reward status? \n\nCurious how close you are to the next milestone? Drop us a note and we’ll follow up.\n\n### How are contributions verified? \n\nContributions are verified by our Developer Advocacy Team. There are no hard rules on what qualifies as a valid contribution. In general, we intend to reward genuine efforts to contribute, not results (e.g. a pull request may be rejected and still earn a reward).\n\n## Getting started as a Sensu Contributor \n\nIf you would you like to contribute to Sensu, but you’re not sure how to get started, drop us a line!\n\n---\n\nTitle: Latest topics - Sensu Community\nURL: https://discourse.sensu.io/\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n| Topic | | Replies | Views | Activity |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| New to Sensu Resources Uncategorized Hi there!
